function.name: read
function.description: Read a file from the workspace. Supports text files, images (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP), plus PDF and HTML documents. DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX files are view-only in the workspace UI. Relative paths use the primary workspace; authorized sibling repositories require their displayed absolute path. Text lines are prefixed with 'NNNNN| ' line numbers — display-only metadata: NEVER include the prefix in edit old_string/new_string or write content. Preferred over shell cat, sed, head, or tail for reading files.

path.description: File path. Relative paths resolve against the primary workspace. For a file in an authorized non-primary repository, use the absolute path shown by the repository map or a prior search result.

limit.description: Max lines to return. Omit for all lines from offset.

function.name: ls
function.description: List immediate children of a directory with type and size. Preferred over shell ls or dir.

function.name: glob
function.description: Find files by glob pattern. Use match='path' (default) for full-path patterns like 'src/**/*.ts', or match='name' for filename-only like '*.py'. Results are sorted by modification time, newest first; a partial page ends with a notice giving the offset for the next page. Preferred over shell find or ls for locating files by name.

pattern.description: Glob pattern. Use '**/*.py' or 'src/**/*.ts' to match by full path, or '*.py' with match='name' to match filename only.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default 200).

offset.description: Skip this many files first. Use the offset a truncation notice gives to fetch the next page.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents by regex (ripgrep). output_mode 'content' (default) returns 'file:line: text'; 'files_with_matches' returns only paths, newest first — start there to locate code; 'count' returns matching lines per file plus a total. Filter with include (filename glob) or type (e.g. 'py'). A partial page ends with a notice giving the offset for the next page. Preferred over shell grep or rg for searching file contents.

pattern.description: Regex to match per line (e.g. 'def main', 'TODO|FIXME').

include.description: Filename glob to filter files (e.g. '*.py'). Default '*'.

type.description: File type to search, as a ripgrep type name (e.g. 'py', 'ts', 'rust'). Faster and broader than include for a language.

output_mode.description: 'content' (default): matching lines as 'file:line: text'. 'files_with_matches': only file paths, newest first — the cheapest way to locate code. 'count': matching lines per file plus a total.

max_results.description: Maximum entries per page: matching lines, files or per-file counts depending on output_mode (default 100, max 1000).

offset.description: Skip this many entries first. Use the offset a truncation notice gives to fetch the next page.

fixed_strings.description: Treat pattern as a literal string, not a regex.

multiline.description: Let the pattern span lines; '.' also matches newlines. Write \r?\n to also match Windows line endings (default false).

context.description: Lines of context to show around each match in content mode, like grep -C (default 0, max 10). Context lines use 'file-line-' prefixes.

function.name: date
function.description: Get the current local date, time, and timezone (e.g. '2026-04-06 14:30:00 ICT').
